reading.name: Norway
reading.headline: Norway is in the Low tier (17/100, 194th riskiest of 203; 49th of 52 in Europe & Central Asia). Among the most stable places in the sample.
reading.ground: Politics rarely disrupts daily life or business. Institutions generally work, disputes go through courts and elections, and the economy has buffers. Risk comes mainly from unexpected shocks. No pillar scores as high risk; the relatively weakest area is Macroeconomic & Financial (33/100).
direction: Over the longer run it has been fairly stable (14 in 2015, 17 now).

business: Use the score to decide where to look closer: compare with peers (Peers tab) and read the drivers before deciding anything.
A relatively stable profile: standard due diligence is usually enough. Watch *Score changes* for early shifts.
ngo: A development setting: focus on long-term programmes and local partners.
travel: Check your government's official travel advice for Norway before you go. It changes far faster than annual data.
research: No pillar is high risk. Ask what keeps Norway stable and what could change that; its weakest area is Macroeconomic & Financial.
Put it in context: Norway ranks 49th of 52 in Europe & Central Asia and the Peers tab shows who is close.
Check whether changes are real: governance moves inside the WGI confidence intervals may be noise (Data tab, Governance).
Test the drivers: the What-if simulator shows which indicators would move the score most.
Write it up: the Assessment builder turns this into a structured brief with probabilities.

caveats: Scores are relative: they show where a country sits among the others and give no probability of any event.
The data look backwards: governance scores describe last year and conflict data lag by up to two years. Check current news and official travel advice.
This is general, educational guidance. It is not investment, legal or security advice.
